memory_versions.text:
Working notes:

- Order form v1 requires: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Normalize source aliases:
  - customer → cust
  - quantity → qty
  - likely abbreviated/truncated “qu…”/“quanti…” → quantity/qty
  - inspect source carefully for priority and shipping-country values before submitting.
- Do not submit while priority or ship_country is absent/invalid; these caused most rejections. A valid quantity alone is insufficient.
- Preserve valid customer, email, and order_date values across retries; repeated batches may represent the same underlying order.
- Each order has up to 3 attempts. After the third rejection, it is routed to manual review; no attempts remain.
- Handwritten/transcribed and partner-portal records may contain incomplete or abbreviated fields. Customer confirmation does not guarantee all required fields are valid.
- ORD-5104 demonstrates that correctly normalizing quantity and supplying valid priority/ship_country can produce acceptance.

Working notes:

- Order forms v1 and v2 require: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Normalize aliases:
  - customer → cust
  - quantity, “qu…”/“quanti…” → qty only when the source contains a valid, recoverable quantity value.
- A field label or abbreviation alone does not make its value valid. Inspect the complete source record; do not guess missing, truncated, or malformed values.
- Priority must be an accepted value. “Ordinary priority” from intake is not necessarily a valid form value; verify the exact allowed representation.
- ship_country must be explicitly present and valid. Never infer it from the customer, sender, portal, or other context.
- Do not submit until priority, qty, and ship_country are all valid; quantity normalization alone is insufficient.
- Preserve valid cust, email, and order_date values across retries. Repeated batches with the same details are likely the same underlying order, not new orders.
- Each order has up to 3 attempts. After the third rejection it goes to manual review; no attempts remain.
- Customer confirmation, duplicate-check claims, and partner-portal origin do not guarantee complete or valid fields.
- Recent records confirm that quantity aliases can still fail when the underlying value is malformed or absent, and that repeated retries without correcting priority/qty/ship_country lead to manual review.

Working notes:

- Order forms v1–v3 require: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Normalize aliases:
  - customer → cust
  - quantity, “qu…”/“quanti…” → qty only when the complete source contains a valid, recoverable quantity.
- A label or abbreviation alone is not a value. Inspect the full source record; never guess from truncated, blank, malformed, or missing data.
- Priority must use the exact accepted form value. “Ordinary priority,” including intake-team annotations, is not confirmed valid.
- ship_country must be explicitly present and valid. Never infer it from customer, sender, portal, handwritten/transcription context, or other metadata.
- Do not submit until priority, qty, and ship_country are valid. Quantity may be valid while priority or ship_country remains invalid; validate each independently.
- Preserve valid cust, email, and order_date across retries. Repeated records with matching details are likely the same order, not new orders, despite duplicate-check claims.
- Customer confirmation, confirmation-email requests, partner-portal origin, and reception transcription do not establish field validity.
- Each order has up to 3 attempts. After the third rejection, it goes to manual review; no attempts remain.
- Recent batches show repeated retries without correcting priority/qty/ship_country cause the same rejection. “Ordinary priority” and absent/invalid ship_country consistently remain blockers.
- Do not treat a partially displayed source or truncated action payload as proof that a field was valid or safely recoverable.

Working notes:

- Order forms v1–v4 require: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Normalize aliases:
  - customer → cust
  - quantity, “qu…”/“quanti…” → qty only when the complete source contains a valid, recoverable quantity.
- A label, abbreviation, partial display, or action payload alone is not a value. Inspect the complete source; never guess from truncated, blank, malformed, or missing data.
- Validate priority, qty, and ship_country independently. Do not submit unless all three are valid.
- Priority must use the exact accepted form value. “Ordinary priority,” including intake-team annotations, remains unconfirmed and invalid.
- ship_country must be explicitly present and valid. Never infer it from customer, sender, portal, handwritten/transcription context, or other metadata.
- Recent v4 batches confirm that repeated retries with truncated/unrecoverable quantity and/or unaccepted priority produce the same rejection. Customer calls, portal origin, reception transcription, and intake annotations do not establish validity.
- A quantity can be valid while priority remains invalid (as seen in ORD-5132–5134); do not reject or accept other fields based on the status of one field.
- Preserve valid cust, email, and order_date across retries. Matching details across records likely indicate the same order despite duplicate-check claims.
- Each order has up to 3 attempts. After the third rejection, send it to manual review; no attempts remain.

Working notes:

- Order forms v1–v5 require: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Normalize aliases:
  - customer → cust
  - quantity, “qu…”/“quanti…” → qty only when the complete source contains a valid, recoverable quantity.
- A label, abbreviation, partial display, or action payload alone is not a value. Inspect the complete source; never guess from truncated, blank, malformed, handwritten/transcribed, or missing data.
- Validate priority, qty, and ship_country independently. Do not submit unless all three are valid.
- Priority must use the exact accepted form value. “Ordinary priority,” including intake-team annotations, remains unconfirmed and invalid.
- ship_country must be explicitly present and valid. Never infer it from customer, sender, portal/front-desk origin, calls, confirmation requests, handwritten/transcription context, or metadata.
- Even visible quantity values (including 1, 11, 110, and 117) remain invalid when the source is incomplete or unrecoverable. Repeated retries with altered/truncated quantities do not establish validity.
- Customer calls, portal/front-desk forwarding, duplicate-check claims, reception transcription, and intake annotations do not establish field validity.
- A quantity can be valid while priority remains invalid; assess each field independently.
- Preserve valid cust, email, and order_date across retries. Matching details across records likely indicate the same order despite duplicate-check claims.
- Each order has up to 3 attempts. After the third rejection, set status to manual_review and preserve available valid fields; no attempts remain.

Working notes:

- Order forms v1–v5 require: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Version 6 requires: cust, contact_email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Normalize customer → cust and email → contact_email for v6; do not submit an obsolete/extra email field when contact_email is required.
- A label, abbreviation, partial display, or action payload alone is not a value. Inspect the complete source; never guess from truncated, blank, malformed, handwritten/transcribed, or missing data.
- Validate priority, qty, and ship_country independently. Do not submit unless all required fields are valid.
- Priority must use the exact accepted form value. “Ordinary priority,” including intake-team annotations, remains unconfirmed and invalid.
- ship_country must be explicitly present and valid. Never infer it from customer, sender, portal/front-desk origin, calls, confirmation requests, handwritten/transcription context, or metadata.
- Quantity is invalid when incomplete or unrecoverable, including displayed values such as 1, 11, 110, or 117. Retries with altered/truncated quantities do not establish validity.
- Customer calls, portal/front-desk forwarding, duplicate-check claims, reception transcription, and intake annotations do not establish field validity.
- A quantity can be valid while priority remains invalid; assess each field independently.
- Preserve valid cust, contact_email/email, and order_date across retries, mapping the email field to the schema’s canonical name. Matching details may indicate the same order despite duplicate-check claims.
- Each order has up to 3 attempts. After the third rejection, set status to manual_review, preserve available valid fields, and make no further attempts.

Working notes:

- Order forms v1–v5 require: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Versions 6–7 require: cust, contact_email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Normalize customer → cust and email → contact_email; never submit obsolete/extra email fields.
- A label, abbreviation, partial display, action payload, error field, or annotation alone is not a value. Inspect the complete source; never guess from truncated, blank, malformed, handwritten/transcribed, or missing data.
- Validate cust, contact_email, order_date, priority, qty, and ship_country independently. Submit only when every required field is valid.
- Priority must use the exact accepted form value. “Ordinary priority,” including intake-team annotations, customer calls, or confirmation claims, is unconfirmed and invalid.
- ship_country must be explicitly present and valid. Never infer it from customer, sender, portal/front-desk origin, calls, confirmation requests, transcription context, or metadata.
- Quantity is invalid when incomplete or unrecoverable, including displayed values such as 1, 11, 110, or 117 when the source is truncated/ambiguous. Retries with altered or truncated quantities do not establish validity.
- Customer calls, portal/front-desk forwarding, duplicate-check claims, reception transcription, and intake annotations do not establish field validity.
- A quantity can be valid while priority remains invalid; assess each field independently.
- Preserve valid cust, contact_email/email, and order_date across retries, mapping email to the schema’s canonical name. Matching details may indicate the same order despite duplicate-check claims.
- Each order has up to 3 attempts. After the third rejection, set status to manual_review, preserve available valid fields, and make no further attempts.
